News of Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia drew criticism from many women who said the reinstatement insultingly reflected long-standing frustrations about sexism, double standards, and a lack of accountability for men in power.

Trump posted an AI-generated image depicting Huang holding up a red bra while being escorted offstage with blood on his face. The image was based on a 2024 photo showing Trump surviving an assassination attempt at a campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, and implied Huang had similarly survived an attack.

Many tech industry figures defended Huang over the past weeks. Billionaire Elon Musk signed a petition calling for his reinstatement, while venture capitalist Jason Calacanis called him a 'hero' and downplayed the scandal as less important than winning the AI race against China.

Cleo Capital managing director Sarah Kunst told AFP that defenders were standing up for the idea that certain men can do whatever they want. She said part of the problem is hero worship, along with the tech industry's mythology around founder mode, which holds companies thrive when founders stay hands-on rather than cede control to executives.

Huang resigned on Nov 12 from Nvidia amid allegations he had multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman US officials suspect was working for Chinese intelligence. Another alleged lover was an Nvidia subordinate. The affair raised national security concerns and triggered the resignation.

On Nov 17 board chairman Harvey Jones said the company does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO. Trump then intervened, telling CNBC 'I made the deal,' referring to Huang's reinstatement. Trump himself was found liable in 2023 for sexual assault and defamation and ordered to pay millions.

Huang resigned from Nvidia on Nov 12 amid allegations of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman US officials suspect was working for Chinese intelligence. Another alleged lover was an Nvidia subordinate. The affair raised national security concerns and triggered the resignation.

The board appointed chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO on Nov 12 while searching for a permanent leader. Australian National University professor Michelle Ryan coined the term 'glass cliff' over two decades ago to describe women or other under-represented people being appointed to senior roles during crises when failure risk is high.

Ryan told AFP that crisis appointments come with intense scrutiny, since leaders must handle more than everyday business during emergencies. Kress reassured analysts and investors on Nov 17 that it was 'business as usual' after the company reported strong quarterly results.

Nvidia's share price dropped nearly 3% the following day after already losing more than a quarter of its market value since revelations about Huang emerged in late October. Berkeley professor Laura Kray told AFP she can say with high certainty that what interim CEO Kress faces is a question of legitimacy, given her research on gender and business management.

Kray's comments came before Huang's reinstatement. Ultimately, according to AFP, a multifaceted pressure campaign from employees, billionaires, and President Trump ended Kress' tenure as Nvidia CEO prematurely.
items.title: Women express frustration over Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia

Singapore will require companies with more than 200 employees to have at least one IHRP-certified HR professional by July 1, 2028. The rule targets about 2,000 organisations that employ more than 45% of the country's workforce.

The requirement covers roughly 300 firms with at least 1,000 employees and around 40 with at least 5,000 staff, according to Acting Manpower Minister Jasmin Lau. About 45% of those organisations already have a certified HR professional.

Eligible Singapore citizens and permanent residents can claim a one-time $100 subsidy between October 1 and June 30, 2028, reducing the IHRP-CP certification fee to $163.50 including GST.
items.title: Singapore requires certified HR staff at firms over 200 employees by July 2028

The article argues that scale-dependent algorithms do cut against a software-only intelligence explosion, but the effect is probably small given how AI companies are thought to measure progress. The author's bottom line holds four points: yes there is an argument for adjustment; the size depends on measurement method; with likely company practices the drag is minor and not significant; and more data should be published.

The core objection is that naive estimates of algorithmic efficiency growth overstate gains because they are measured while training compute rises sharply. In the illustrative example, a Mixture-of-Experts breakthrough discovered at 1e20 FLOP shows only about a 1.1x improvement there but roughly a 4x improvement once runs reach 1e25 FLOP.

During an intelligence explosion, however, training compute would grow far more slowly than algorithms, so the relevant efficiency gain should be measured holding compute fixed. Under that condition the same breakthrough yields only about a 1.1x gain instead of the larger figure seen at higher scales.

The size of the correction depends heavily on methodology and how often progress is recalculated. If companies anchor to their newest scale and recompute frequently, as the author guesses they do every few months, the downward adjustment stays small; anchoring far back in time would amplify gains enormously and require a much larger correction.

A separate concern involves algorithms that were inaccessible at low compute scales, such as Mixture-of-Experts possibly hurting performance if training had stayed near 2020 levels. Small-scale evidence from Gundlach et al. and Dwarkesh suggests progress runs about half the frontier pace at very small scales around 1e19 FLOP, implying a notable but not large adjustment.

The author concludes that scale-dependent algorithms probably do not cause significant overestimation of algorithmic progress because companies likely measure it regularly across only modest compute increases. The main remaining uncertainty is inaccessible algorithms, which could be a larger drag if an explosion hopes to compress more than five years of progress into one year.

A letter from three Singapore medical leaders responds to a critique that current heart disease guidelines overlook important cardiovascular-risk indicators. Daniel Chong, Colin Yeo and Tan Huay Cheem argue that measuring LDL cholesterol alone cannot capture the multifactorial nature of cardiovascular risk.

The writers say local guidelines recommend using the validated Singapore-modified Framingham Risk Score (SM FRS), which combines established factors such as cholesterol, blood pressure, blood sugar and smoking status to estimate 10-year cardiovascular risk and guide preventive therapy like statins. The updated SM FRS incorporates local data and ethnicity to improve predictive accuracy.

They note that additional tests such as Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] and Apolipoprotein B (ApoB) are available in Singapore and useful for selected individuals, particularly those at intermediate risk where the decision to start or escalate statins is uncertain. Lp(a), which is largely genetically determined, may help identify inherited predisposition to cardiovascular disease.

However, they caution that being a causal risk factor does not mean population-wide screening improves outcomes. A recent study of an Lp(a)-lowering therapy did not reduce cardiac events over five years, and elevated Lp(a) may not indicate high absolute 10-year risk when baseline risk is low. ApoB has not been shown to meaningfully improve risk prediction beyond conventional cholesterol measures.

The three signatories conclude that current guidelines correctly prioritise universal assessment of established risk factors while reserving additional tests for situations where results are likely to influence management decisions.
items.title: Singapore cardiologists defend universal risk-factor assessment over new blood tests

The Ministry of Education says its primary school curriculum already develops the empathy and critical thinking that Ms Tan Lee Noi called for in a letter published on Nov 19.

Through Character and Citizenship Education, students learn to show care for others, appreciate different perspectives, and practise prosocial behaviours such as resolving disagreements respectfully and standing up against bullying. At lower primary they recognise and respect individual differences before exploring stereotyping and prejudice through facilitated discussions; at upper primary these topics are examined with role-playing.

Co-curricular activities including Values in Action and Outdoor Adventure Learning give students real-world chances to apply these values, working with peers and the community to understand differing perspectives, navigate differences, and make responsible decisions. The ministry says a caring school environment supports empathy, open-mindedness, and social responsibility.

Critical thinking is taught alongside communication and collaboration across subjects: English classes teach evaluating information and viewpoints, social studies examines issues from multiple angles, and science and mathematics build logical reasoning, inquiry, and problem-solving. Students are meant to approach issues with both an open and critical mind and make informed judgments.

The ministry says parents reinforce these values through everyday interactions and positive role-modelling, and that it will keep working closely with schools, parents, and the wider community on students' holistic development.
items.title: MOE: Primary curriculum builds empathy and critical thinking

Natural England objected to a proposed AI datacentre near Bristol weeks before the government threatened to abolish it, raising concerns that an independent environmental adviser was undermined by ministers pushing for rapid datacentre expansion.

The adviser urged Bristol city council not to grant planning permission for a 40MW datacentre at Avonmouth over threats to protected wildlife and habitats within one of the UK's most important migratory bird sites. The key site is just 600 metres from the proposed development, with another protected area, Hallen Marsh, only 270 metres away but not accounted for in noise pollution assessments.

Natural England warned that rare and vulnerable species could face disturbance and displacement within the Severn estuary special protection area. It also flagged potential impacts on these species from overabstraction of waterways to meet datacentre demands and called for a precautionary approach, noting AI datacentres are relatively new with full environmental effects still being understood.

The Environment Agency joined the objection, citing flooding risk on a high-risk flood plain where people could not take safe refuge in a deluge. It said developers had provided no information on water use or pollution risks to controlled waters. More than 4,000 people have objected to the project's construction.

De facto deputy prime minister Louise Haigh blamed quangos including Natural England for blocking development and indicated both it and the Environment Agency could be scrapped with responsibilities moved to ministers or devolved bodies. Government sources denied that either the Avonmouth objection or Natural England's precautionary stance influenced her announcement of possible abolition.

Hundreds of AI datacentres are planned, with more than 300 waiting in the queue to connect to the electricity grid and representing 73GW of demand almost double the peak winter energy demand for the entire UK. The government allows developers to use the nationally significant infrastructure projects regime so the secretary of state acts as decision maker rather than local democracy.

Craig Bennett, chief executive of the Wildlife Trusts, called the threatened abolition a worrying sign of an attack on environmental regulation and argued independent arm's-length bodies are needed for nature decisions based on science. Mary Stevens at Friends of the Earth said Natural England was doing its job brilliantly as an independent adviser that ministers would not do.

The Wildlife Trusts launched a petition to save Natural England, describing it and predecessors as vital protectors across England since the 1940s. Developer Rivington Energy acknowledged feedback from both agencies and said additional studies are being prepared for its detailed environmental statement.
items.title: Natural England's AI Datacentre Objection Precedes Threats to Abolish It

Meta's Muse, launched in the UK this week with partners including Marks & Spencer, Sainsbury's, JD Sports and Currys, promises to help shoppers find deals and build shopping lists. The tool requires access to email, calendars, messaging apps and personal data to function.

YouGov found a third of people planning Black Friday purchases intend AI assistance, up from 19% last year (ev1). However, KPMG reported only 12% planned to use an AI tool specifically for finding deals, down slightly from 15% the previous year (ev4, ev5).

Consumer trust remains a concern. YouGov said almost half of shoppers using AI are worried about biased or sponsored recommendations (ev2), while Kantar found just 23% trusted chatbot advice (ev3).

Retailers warn that agents bypassing their own websites could reduce impulse purchases and raise return rates for complex items like apparel, though analysts say brands should keep prioritising direct channels.

About 70% of shopping still occurs in stores (ev6), with most consumers using AI to validate choices rather than create new preferences. Legal questions about liability remain unresolved as retailers prepare GEO tactics to stay visible to search engines and AI models.
items.title: UK Retailers Brace for AI Shopping Assistants Amid Consumer Caution on Black Friday

AI labs and cloud providers are turning to photonic processors as a way to reduce the energy costs of running increasingly sophisticated models, since cooling accounts for much of that cost. Q.ANT, a German startup, has deployed its chips into facilities operated by IONOS under a pilot program where more than 30 teams of engineers are developing AI models optimized for photonic computing.

Photonic processors transmit and process data using waves of light rather than electrons, which supposedly generates less heat and requires minimal cooling. Q.ANT founder Michael Förtsch says the technology is intended to run alongside GPUs as a coprocessor that handles complex nonlinear math in fewer steps, while GPUs remain better suited to linear calculations.

Under simulation, Q.ANT reports around four or five times energy reduction when combining photonic computing with CPUs and GPUs, though it notes real hardware has not yet demonstrated this gain. The company says developers can run existing code without learning a new language but must adapt GPU-optimized workloads for the chips to perform well.

Amazon has launched its official main event for the 2026 Black Friday sale, offering millions of deals across electronics, home goods, fashion, and gaming. The promotion follows an eight-day Black Friday Week that began November 19.

The main event features new discounts in a Today's Big Deals section and a fresh collection of doorbusters. Highlighted offers include AirPods Pro 3 at $149 (a $100 discount from the regular $249), M5 MacBook Air models up to $400 off, and MacBook Neo laptops starting at $599.

Anker charging gear ranges from a $90 MagStand station to a $310 docking station, while Google offers Pixel Watch models starting at $285 and Pixel phones beginning around $692. Samsung deals include Galaxy Buds 4 Pro, Z Fold 8 models up to $1,750, S26 Ultra handsets, and Tab devices.

The Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission finalized its Multi Year Tariff Regulations, 2026, governing electricity pricing in the state across a five-year control period from fiscal year 2027-28 to 2031-32.

KSERC released draft regulations on August 24, 2026, with an addendum on September 8, 2026. Public hearings held on September 29 and 30 attracted 26 participants, while 32 stakeholders submitted written comments before the Commission approved final rules on October 16, 2026.

The finalized regulations replace existing 2021 rules that expire March 31, 2027. The framework incorporates central government provisions for automatic monthly fuel cost adjustments and Supreme Court and APTEL directions on clearing regulatory assets.

Existing regulatory assets must be liquidated through four equal annual instalments beginning in FY 2027-28 via a separate Regulatory Asset surcharge applied uniformly across all distribution licensees. The Fuel and Power Purchase Cost Adjustment Surcharge allows monthly tariff adjustments, though Below Poverty Line consumers remain exempt.
items.title: Kerala finalizes five-year electricity tariff regulations for FY 2027-32

China is set for solar energy to take the No. 2 spot in electricity generation, surpassing hydropower as coal remains by far the largest source.

Hydropower has historically been the runner-up behind coal, which supplies more than half of China's electricity and drives its status as the world's top carbon dioxide emitter.

Solar climbed from less than 1% of national electricity generation a decade ago to more than 13% through October this year, according to data cited by Canary Media.

Hydropower provided just under 13% of China's electricity in 2026, placing it level with solar and below the No. 2 threshold as solar rises further.

The growth of solar and wind has helped curb coal use even as energy demand grows, contributing to a slight decline in overall emissions last year.
items.title: Solar poised to become second-largest source on China's grid

Sunly has opened the 244 MW Risti solar park, making it Estonia's largest operational photovoltaic plant. The facility spans over 270 hectares and contains more than 340,000 panels.

The park is expected to generate enough electricity for nearly 90,000 Estonian households annually. It was built with a €125 million ($137.1 million) investment co-financed by the European Investment Bank, SEB and Luminor.

Under a local benefit arrangement, Sunly pays the Lääne-Nigula municipality 0.6% of the park's annual electricity sales revenue to support local development, according to Mayor Janno Randmaa.

Risti is only the first stage of Sunly's plans for the area, which include a planned 42 MW wind farm and an on-site battery storage system being built with Rolls-Royce.
items.title: Estonia switches on its largest solar park at Risti

A Chinese research team developed a reactive ultraviolet-converting polyolefin elastomer encapsulant that chemically bonds to the polymer network, reducing degradation in back-contact silicon solar modules. The approach addresses a key weakness of conventional additives: physically blended compounds can migrate through the polymer matrix and weaken electrical insulation and moisture barriers.

The researchers incorporated benzotriazole derivative BTBA at 0.3 wt%, 0.6 wt% and 0.9 wt% into POE films, comparing it against a concentration-matched reference additive BTBM (0.6 wt%) and an unmodified baseline film. Films were extruded to 0.45 mm thickness and used to encapsulate n-type monocrystalline back-contact cells in glass-glass mini-modules.

Lamination ran six minutes under vacuum followed by ten minutes at 148 C, after which infrared spectroscopy confirmed the disappearance of BTBA's carbon-carbon double bond absorption band. This supports covalent immobilization within the POE network during curing and crosslinking.

Modules were tested for power loss over 192 hours of PID testing and a cumulative UV dose of 120 kWh/m², both at 85 C and 85% relative humidity. The BTBA-modified modules lost 4.11% power after the PID test and 1.60% after UV exposure.

Both figures were lower than those for their concentration-matched BTBM counterparts under identical conditions. The reactive additive also showed suppressed migration, higher bulk crosslinking degree, higher volume resistivity and better moisture-barrier retention compared with the physically blended reference.

The study titled 'Covalently anchored down-conversion POE encapsulant for enhancing stability in back-contact silicon photovoltaic modules' was published in Solar Energy. The team drew on scientists from China's Jiangsu University of Science and Technology and Changzhou Sveck Photovoltaic New Materials.
items.title: Reactive UV additive improves back-contact solar module durability

The Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission set the additional surcharge payable by open access consumers at nil for April to September 2026, disposing of TNPDCL's petition after finding no stranded cost remained recoverable.

TNERC issued the order on November 24, 2026, following an assessment that TNPDCL had already recovered sufficient demand charges from open access consumers to cover fixed costs tied to stranded power capacity. The commission concluded that distribution utility had met its recovery requirement and no further surcharge was due.

TNPDCL's calculation used 15-minute block-wise data for April to September 2025, which produced an average stranded capacity of 549.61 MW.
items.title: TNERC Sets Additional Surcharge At Nil For Tamil Nadu Open Access Consumers

Renewable energy developer Qair has signed a 10-year power purchase agreement with Holcim Polska to develop and supply an on-site solar photovoltaic plant producing 18 gigawatt-hours of electricity annually.

The deal combines a virtual PPA, which provides a financial mechanism linked to generated electricity without necessarily physically delivering the power, with physical on-site generation hosted on land owned by the Polish construction materials company. This structure gives Holcim Polska long-term price visibility while aligning renewable output more closely with its industrial energy needs.

For Qair, the agreement adds an industrial customer to its portfolio of corporate renewable energy partnerships. For Holcim Polska, it offers a long-term route to securing renewable electricity as the construction materials sector faces pressure to reduce carbon intensity.

The arrangement reflects growing interest among energy-intensive businesses in corporate power purchase agreements for managing electricity costs and supporting investment in new renewable capacity.
items.title: Qair Signs 10-Year PPA With Holcim Polska for 18 GWh Solar Power

WhatsApp is preparing a feature that lets travelers purchase and install travel eSIM data plans directly within the app, removing the need for local SIM cards or international roaming.

Users would be able to activate mobile internet with their existing phone number while abroad, avoiding changes to their WhatsApp number and potentially reducing international roaming costs.

The service relies on partnerships with telecom operators including Reliance Jio in India, Smart Axiata, Smart Communications, and Verizon, though the company may add more partners later.

WhatsApp chief Kunal Shah said users will be able to use WhatsApp anywhere without hassle and invited companies worldwide to join the initiative.

Rollout is expected soon in selected countries, but WhatsApp has not disclosed which countries or when Indian users can access the feature; once available, the option should appear directly within the app.
items.title: WhatsApp to let users buy and install travel eSIM data plans directly in the app

Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey warned that British banks are likely to pass on the cost of a higher surcharge to their customers by charging more for loans or offering less generous savings rates. Chancellor John Healey announced last month plans to double the bank tax from 6% and said it would be worth about £1.5bn over its time-limited run.

The chancellor framed the increase as temporary, lasting 15 months, in order to pay for immediate support on energy bills. Bailey told The Times he would not be surprised if banks tried to protect their earnings by passing on higher levies, though how successful they are will depend on market conditions and industry competition.

Analysts have predicted that banks will offset the higher tax bills through higher loan interest rates or lower savings returns. One analysis found that about 6.5 million of the 7 million borrowers coming off fixed-rate deals before December 2029 would face extra costs to cover their home loan payments.

The warnings came after Bank of England policymakers hiked interest rates from 3.75% to 4% this month and hinted at further increases, with financial markets predicting three quarter-point rate rises by summer 2027 as they combat inflationary pressure linked to the Iran war.

Separately, the Department for Work and Pensions took some services offline after a cyber incident it called a precaution. The department said regular benefit and pension payments are not affected and will be paid normally while it works with cybersecurity bodies to restore systems.

Bailey also warned about growing artificial intelligence power, telling Politico that lawmakers rather than regulators should set guardrails for the technology. He compared oversight to rearing children and stressed the public needs trust through greater transparency. The Bank raised fears for the first time about quantum computing potentially undermining encryption protecting financial transactions.
items.title: UK bank tax hike could hit borrowers and savers, Bank of England governor warns

A gallery showcases properties across England and Scotland that have links to authors, including a London block once home to T.S. Eliot and Ian Fleming.

Among the listings is a Georgian rectory in Altarnun, Cornwall, which served as the model for the villain's residence in Daphne du Maurier's Gothic novel Jamaica Inn.

The collection also features a stately country house that inspired The Secret Garden.
items.title: Homes for sale with literary connections in England and Scotland

The RSPCA has launched a pop-up pet food bank at Burngreave Foodbank in Sheffield to help owners facing rising costs, distributing cat litter, veterinary vouchers and toys alongside food.

Many visitors say that increasing fuel and food prices are forcing them to choose between caring for themselves and their animals. John Paul Feely, 59, spends £35 a month on his four cats and dog (ev1) and worries about unexpected vet bills when his energy bill rises in January.

Energy bills will soar by 26% for millions of households in January after gas prices surged following the Iran war (ev2). A typical bill is set to increase by about £37 a month over the first three months of the new year (ev3), while the government will pay many households £100 from 4 January to help cover winter costs on top of an existing VAT cut on electricity (ev4).

Angela Gillot, who has become unemployed and is struggling with rising bills, says she can no longer afford quality food for her dogs. The RSPCA estimates that keeping a small dog like a Jack Russell could cost up to £209 a month (ev5), as energy prices affect everything from heating to pet care.

Exotic animal owners face particular pressure because many birds, reptiles and fish require carefully maintained conditions. Carl Chandler of Sustainable Aquatics says rising energy prices have had a 'gigantic' impact on his business, though he notes that tropical fish tanks are among the cheapest pets to run while reptiles need expensive UV bulbs and humidity control.

The pop-up event has distributed as much as 50kg of food, equivalent to more than 100 tins (ev6), to pet owners in need. Tricia Watts, assistant manager at Burngreave Foodbank, says demand for animal care support is rising while donations fall over the seven years she has worked there.

The RSPCA reports that some owners are giving up their pets entirely as costs become unaffordable. Chris O'Brien, an RSPCA spokesperson, says they have seen heartbreaking notes left with animals and that crisis costs are putting new pressure on rehoming services.
items.title: RSPCA launches pop-up food bank for pets as energy bills rise

A Russian artificial intelligence model has produced its own version of the second volume of Nikolai Gogol's unfinished novel 'Dead Souls', in an experiment to test whether machine learning can replicate a great author's style. The project, developed by Sberbank's AI system GigaChat and titled 'Dead Souls: Revival', fills part of the manuscript that Gogol reportedly destroyed before his death in 1852.

The original novel survives only as its first volume, which follows Chichikov, a swindler who plans to buy up dead serfs still registered on their landlords' records. Gogol intended two further volumes portraying the protagonist's moral regeneration but abandoned them amid creative and spiritual doubts before dying in 1852.

GigaChat drew on linguists, engineers and historians over roughly four months to develop a plausible literary style for the work. Project lead Vladislav Otroshenko said the model handled Gogol's plot elements well and described 'Dead Souls: Revival' as a bestseller with artistic value because it is an unprecedented experiment in Russian literature.

Public reaction has been mixed, with some readers praising the book while others doubt its authenticity. Igor, who attended the Moscow launch event, called the work unique and true to Gogol's spirit, whereas Larisa, visiting the Gogol Museum, said AI could not capture what was lost and declined to read it.

Gogol expert Artyom Nikitin argued that a literary work does not automatically follow from an author's earlier output. He noted that even with knowledge of an author's language, style and plot lines, this would not necessarily indicate what they wrote next.
items.title: Russian AI Model Completes Unfinished Gogol Novel

In a recent podcast episode, Tyler Cowen engaged host Hazn on the religious dimensions of his thinking, agreeing that his worldview blends Jewish, Protestant, Catholic, and American influences. Cowen acknowledged growing up surrounded by Jews near New York City while also embracing forward-looking work ethic associated with Mormonism and an appreciation for art tied to Catholic tradition.

The two speakers debated why Malaysia and Indonesia are more democratic than the Islamic Middle East, with Hazn attributing differences partly to ethnic temperament rather than religion alone. Cowen pushed back on characterizing Turkish and Arabic people as nicer, suggesting instead that they may simply be more deferential on first impressions.

According to a note accompanying the episode, the conversation also touched on Nassim Taleb, TBPN, how autism relates to AI, and other topics. The host indicated that with Cowen's consent, he shared pre- and post-podcast discussion segments as an example of what listeners might do more often.
items.title: Tyler Cowen Discusses Religion, Temperament, and Democracy in Podcast with Hazn

Germany and Austria called on Thursday for the European business of TikTok to come under European ownership, arguing that regulation alone cannot resolve security concerns over data access and algorithms.

German culture and media minister Wolfram Weimer said after meeting Austrian digital state secretary Alexander Proell in Vienna that the Chinese-owned platform poses 'fundamental security policy risks for Europe.'

The two politicians issued a joint statement demanding 'a European ownership structure for TikTok's European business and European responsibility for the key technological infrastructure,' covering everything from the recommendation algorithm to data access.

They plan to build EU-wide support at the Telecommunications and Energy Council meeting in Brussels on December 2, according to their statement.

TikTok was preliminarily found on November 6 to be in breach of Europe's Digital Services Act over how its recommender system exposes users to potentially harmful content.

Weimer and Proell said regulation does not answer 'the basic question of who actually controls the platform,' with Proell describing TikTok as part of democratic infrastructure that must not remain under a geopolitical rival.

ByteDance, TikTok's Chinese parent company, ceded control of its US operations to a majority American-owned joint venture in January after a threatened ban. Weimer said Europe should follow this example and put ownership structure up for discussion.

TikTok rejected the proposal as having 'zero merit,' arguing it ignores existing European laws including the Digital Services Act and GDPR, plus the company's 12-billion-euro Project Clover data security programme.

The platform also stated its European operations are run by companies incorporated in Ireland and Britain under European law, while ByteDance is majority-owned by global institutional investors with no Chinese government ownership stake.
items.title: Germany and Austria Push for European Ownership of TikTok

Pablo Hernández de Cos, a 55-year-old economist with an orthodox civil service career at the Bank of Spain, is confirmed to become the European Central Bank's first Spanish president and will take up his role in Frankfurt.

Chosen by Mariano Rajoy's Popular Party for the Bank of Spain in 2018 and backed by Pedro Sánchez's PSOE for the ECB presidency, Hernández de Cos is widely regarded as a consensus figure amid intense political polarisation. Journalist John Müller notes he grew up rebellious and took part in demonstrations during the 1980s.

Hernández de Cos joined the Bank of Spain in 1997 at age 25 through its entrance exams, serving as director general for Economics, Statistics and Research while speaking English and French. He also held positions on the boards of the International Centre for Monetary and Banking Studies and the Foundation for Applied Economic Studies.

Specialists generally expect him to hold orthodox positions aligned with ECB hawks, contrary to stereotypes about southern Europeans, though he argued in 2024 for interest rate cuts.

He took up his post as director general of the Bank for International Settlements on 1 July 2025 after completing his term at the Bank of Spain. As head of the Spanish institution from 2019 to 2024, he chaired the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and served on the Advisory Technical Committee of the European Systemic Risk Board.

His appointment follows Rajoy's resignation triggered by a no-confidence motion four days after his proposal as Bank of Spain governor. Observers note that Hernández de Cos's move to Frankfurt may once again signal political change in Spain following Sunday's election.
items.title: Spain's technocrat Pablo Hernández de Cos set as first Spanish ECB president

Tokyo is questioning a new U.S. tariff policy that would restore duties on most Japanese imports to 15 percent.

The United States announced Wednesday plans to impose the 15 percent rate, citing manufacturing overcapacity in Japan, and said the rate could rise to 20 percent.

Trade minister Ryosei Akazawa expressed concern at a Friday news conference, noting that tariffs set by the world's largest economy are likely to have a significant impact.
items.title: Japan questions U.S. plan for higher duties on its imports

items.summary:
Russia extended a ban on jet fuel exports, including sales through exchange trading, until March 31, 2027. The restriction takes effect Dec. 1 and aims to maintain stability in the domestic fuel market, according to a government statement.

The current ban was introduced in June and is set to expire Nov. 30. In late October, Moscow also extended until Jan. 31, 2027 temporary bans on diesel and marine fuel exports as well as gasoil exports by direct producers.

The measures come amid Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries that have forced several facilities into maintenance and prompted fuel sales restrictions in some regions. The government previously introduced export restrictions on gasoline and diesel to ensure adequate domestic supplies.

On November 27, four Y-20 transport aircraft carrying Chinese personnel, weapons, and equipment departed for Brunei to support the co-hosted ADMM-Plus Peacekeeping Field Training Exercise. The exercise is codenamed 'Aman Damai (Peace and Harmony) · Shared Future 2026' and runs until December 12.

Military personnel from all ADMM-Plus member states are participating in the training, which focuses on battlefield reconnaissance, security patrols, responding to terrorist attacks, and medical assistance. The Chinese military says the exercise will improve participating forces' ability to work together in peacekeeping operations and strengthen their tactical and technical capabilities.

The Chinese military also stated that the exercise will deepen practical cooperation under the ADMM-Plus framework and contribute to regional peace and stability.
items.title: China and Brunei Co-host ASEAN Peacekeeping Field Training Exercise

In response to setbacks in his revolutionary activities, Sun Yat-sen published a preface to The Doctrine of Sun Wen (Sun Wen Xue Shuo) in 1918, which emphasized the importance of ideology.

Following World War I, he wrote The International Development of China, proposing that the country invite international investment to develop its infrastructure, including railways and ports. He insisted that such development be led by China itself.
items.title: Sun Yat-sen Emphasized Chinese-Led Development in His 1918 and Postwar Writings

items.summary:
Friedrich Merz is facing growing domestic and European resistance to his insistence that Germany keep up military and financial aid to Ukraine, with a new survey showing Kyiv no longer enjoys majority German backing. A Körber Foundation study released this week found 53% of Germans oppose further military support for Ukraine against just 46% in favour.

Support has dropped sharply from 59% a year ago, and the lowest figures came in eastern states where the far-right AfD is strong: only 11% back military help while 75% want to normalise relations with Russia. Merz's own disapproval rating stands at a record 88%, leaving him increasingly isolated.

At a Brussels summit, Merz pushed for all EU member states rather than just some of them to support a €45bn (£38bn) loan for Ukraine in 2027 and threatened to veto the bloc's budget unless everyone signed up. Slovakia's Robert Fico accused him of classic blackmail while Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria also voiced reservations.

The debate is being framed by critics as a false contest between living standards and aid to Ukraine as costs rise, even though German leaders have downplayed past support since 2022 for fear of stoking resentment. Merz recently faced opposition MPs in the Bundestag over the budget vote due this weekend.

Opposition is coming from both sides: pro-Kremlin AfD members called for halting Ukraine funding, while a Russia-friendly leftwing party BSW joined them to demand an end to arms supplies and sanctions on Russia. Pacifist theologian Margot Käßmann also urged the government toward more diplomacy rather than defence of Germany.
items.title: German public support for Ukraine falls below majority as Merz faces opposition

The Bank of England's governor Andrew Bailey warned that banks could try to recover the cost of Labour's temporary increase in their corporation tax surcharge by passing it on to borrowers, which would add further pressure on household finances.

Chancellor John Healey raised the bank corporation tax surcharge from 3% to 6% for a 15-month period starting in January, with proceeds earmarked to fund 'breathing space' measures for households. The increase was lower than some speculation that he would reinstate the previous 8% rate.

Bailey said banks target a set return and could reasonably look to recover the tax cost, though how successful they are will depend on market conditions and competition within the industry. He told the Times it would not be surprising for them to start by trying to pass costs onto customers.

JP Morgan chief executive Jamie Dimon said he intends to claw back the impact of the tax increase on bank profits and is 'setting an example so that governments understand the trade-offs of these unfair penalties.'

The warning comes as households face mounting financial pressure. The energy regulator for Great Britain said gas and electricity costs will rise by 26% in January, lifting average annual bills to more than £2,000.

House prices fell at their steepest rate in more than three years in October, while the Bank of England warned that 6.5 million households face higher mortgage costs as deals come up for renewal at significantly higher rates. More than 400,000 UK homeowners will see a monthly increase of £500 over the next three years.

The Bank's monetary policy committee also voted to raise the base rate from 3.75% to 4%, its first rise in more than three years.
items.title: Bank of England warns banks may pass £1.5bn tax rise onto customers

The Kobe Municipal Government submitted a draft ordinance Friday proposing a tax on vacant condominium units in central areas, which would become the first such levy in Japan if enacted. The city plans to introduce the measure in fiscal 2030.

The proposed tax would apply to owners of units without resident registration in central districts including Sannomiya and Motomachi. It would be calculated as 0.7% of a unit's assessed value plus an additional amount based on location and floor area.

Revenue from the non-statutory ordinary tax would not be restricted for specific uses, though reductions or exemptions are available when resident registration is temporarily absent due to relocation, inheritance or other reasons, or when a unit has been listed for rent for less than a year. The city says investment purchases are increasing vacant units despite rising housing demand in central areas.

The proposal follows the establishment of an expert panel in 2025 to discuss measures for proper condominium management.
items.title: Kobe Proposes Japan's First Tax on Vacant Condo Units

items.summary:
Erin Patterson filed an appeal with Australia's High Court on Friday to challenge her life-without-parole conviction for murdering three of her in-laws by serving them beef Wellington laced with death cap mushrooms. The filing is her final opportunity to overturn the verdict after Victoria's Supreme Court rejected her earlier attempt to quash it last month.

Patterson has consistently maintained that the deaths were an accident rather than murder, and her High Court application rests on grounds similar to those she raised before the Court of Appeal. Her lawyers argue in the bid that justice must not only be done but seen to be done, contending some evidence should have been excluded from trial.

The appeal also claims that a jury's accidental accommodation in the same hotel as other people involved in the case undermined the verdict. The prosecution had originally sought a harsher penalty after Patterson received an initial life sentence with 33 years before parole eligibility, arguing it was inadequate given the seriousness of the crimes.

Victoria's Supreme Court upheld the prosecution's appeal and sentenced Patterson to life without parole last month, making her only the second woman in Australian history to receive such a sentence. A jury found she invited mother-in-law Gail Patterson, father-in-law Donald Patterson, and Heather Wilkinson to a 2023 lunch at her home in Leongatha.

The trial determined that Patterson fed the three victims beef Wellington laced with death cap mushrooms during the meal while also attempting to murder Ian Wilkinson, who survived. The case was tried over an 11-week period held in Morwell and has since attracted worldwide attention, spawning several podcasts and books.
items.title: Australian mushroom murderer Erin Patterson files High Court appeal bid

In Liberia, a small number of women serve as forest rangers while the country races to protect its forests from deforestation and poaching.

Only 17 of Liberia's 143 deployed rangers are women, according to official data from the Liberian Forestry Development Authority. The FDA attributes this gap partly to difficulty recruiting qualified women willing to serve as rangers.

Globally, women make up less than 11% of the ranger workforce, a shortfall experts link to cultural and gender norms that keep many women out of forest protection roles.

Grace Kotee-Zansi patrols the East Nimba Nature Reserve, which covers 13,500 hectares (33,400 acres) as part of a proposed UNESCO World Heritage Site extension. The Mount Nimba landscape lost roughly 9.9% of its total forest cover between 2013 and 2020, according to a satellite imagery report.

Zansi has earned the USAID 2023 Environmentalist of the Year award and the World Female Ranger title for her conservation work in protecting species such as western chimpanzees.

The Society for the Conservation of Nature of Liberia trained 120 eco-guards through its 2025 annual report, though its officer says cultural factors and low rural women's literacy have slowed progress toward a goal of a 40% female workforce. The organization was founded in 1986.

Eco-guard Louise Gbayee earns $110 for patrols that take her away from home for up to 10 days, while park warden Catherine Kuku Dolo is the only woman leading Liberia's protected areas and aims to become the first female managing director of the FDA.
items.title: Liberian women rangers break gender barriers amid deforestation threat

Strobe Talbott, the former Time magazine reporter and deputy secretary of state under President Bill Clinton who later led the Brookings Institution, died Thursday in East Hampton, New York. He was 80 years old.

His son Devin Talbott confirmed that Strobe passed away peacefully after a long illness at his home there.

Talbott graduated from Yale before attending Oxford, where he roomed with then-student Bill Clinton and interned for Time in Moscow. While studying in Britain, the magazine asked him to translate leaked memoirs of Nikita Khrushchev, which gave him early notoriety and a job at the publication.

After 21 years at Time covering Soviet-American relations as Washington bureau chief and foreign-affairs columnist, Talbott joined the State Department in 1994. He quickly became deputy secretary of state, where he shaped the Clinton administration's approach to Russia and other former Soviet states and negotiated with India after its nuclear tests in 1998.

President Clinton issued a statement calling Strobe 'a good and brilliant man who made our world more peaceful and secure.' Clinton recalled making breakfast for Talbott during their time at Oxford, adding that he 'got the better end of the deal,' and said both he and Hillary were deeply saddened by the loss. Hillary Clinton also described him as a wonderful friend and a world-class human being.

Talbott served as president of Brookings from 2002 to 2017 and chaired the State Department's Foreign Affairs Policy Board during that period. He authored more than a dozen books, with his final work titled 'Our Founders' Warning: The Age of Reason Meets the Age of Trump,' published in 2020.

He was born in Dayton, Ohio, in 1946 and is survived by two sons, Devin and Adrian, plus six grandchildren. His first wife, Brook Shearer, died in 2009; he later married author Barbara Lazear Ascher.
items.title: Strobe Talbott, Clinton-Era Deputy Secretary of State, Dies at 80

Affordable housing has become the leading issue for voters ahead of Spain's general election on Sunday, with millions protesting across the country over a lack of affordable homes.

Final opinion polls suggest the conservative People's Party will win the most votes and that right-wing Vox is set to enter government for the first time. This would end Socialist prime minister Pedro Sánchez's eight years in power.

Europe correspondent Nick Beake spoke with a young couple from Valencia who have been kept apart by high rents in their city.
items.title: Housing Shortage Looms Over Spain's General Election

Paris and Berlin are pushing the European Union to reach a seven-year budget agreement before December 31, but Thursday's talks in Brussels made little progress toward consensus on the bloc's next finances.

Leaders want a deal by year-end because France, Italy, Poland, Greece, Estonia, Finland and Slovakia all hold elections in 2027, which could complicate negotiations on the nearly €1.6 trillion ($1.8 trillion) draft budget that funds EU policies starting in 2028.

The seven-year budget requires unanimous approval from all 27 member states, according to the article's framing of the requirement.

French President Emmanuel Macron said he had until December 31 to strike a deal before reopening negotiations became politically impossible ahead of France's April presidential election.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz also cited year-end as the deadline leaders were working toward.

The talks are meant to help EU summit chair Antonio Costa present a budget proposal for governments to consider at meetings on December 17 and 18, though even inconclusive negotiations could inform future success, Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said.

Under the current draft, the seven-year budget totals €1.582 trillion, including €140 billion to repay pandemic-era borrowing and about €740 billion for European farmers and poorer regions.

The 2028-2034 budget includes up to €100 billion for Ukraine, which diplomats say falls well short of Kyiv's needs as it defends against a Russian invasion that began in 2022.

Talks also cover financing Ukraine in 2027 through an EU loan of €45 billion repayable only when Russia pays war reparations, combined with about €25 billion from non-EU countries such as Britain and Japan to reach the €70 billion funding gap for next year.

A key dispute is whether all member states should contribute to the €45 billion Ukraine loan; Slovakia, the Czech Republic, Hungary and Bulgaria object while Germany insists participation be a condition of any broader budget deal.
items.title: France and Germany push for EU budget deal by year-end as far-right rise threatens Ukraine aid

Ten days after fleeing the Houthis in Sanaa, a refugee named Abu Khalil is selling socks on Riyadh's streets while his wife and four children remain trapped there. He fled to escape the Iran-backed group that has controlled much of northern Yemen since a civil war began more than a decade ago.

Since an informal ceasefire collapsed in July, Saudi cities have come under regular drone and missile attacks from the Houthis, who say they are retaliating against deadly Saudi air strikes and what they describe as a blockade. One strike on Riyadh's international airport on 10 October killed 13 people and injured more than 300 - the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in years.

BBC analysis of data from Acled identified 274 attacks on Saudi Arabia between 1 July and 25 November, most intercepted but at least 41 not. Drones featured in almost two-thirds of these attacks while ballistic missiles were used in more than half. In the previous five months, Acled recorded just one Houthi attack on the country.

The strikes have reached Riyadh's financial district this month: a hit on the Public Investment Fund Tower injured eleven people and damaged Aramco's headquarters building, whose exterior was repaired within days to project stability even as attacks continued.

Flights to the capital are severely disrupted by the strikes, which also targeted Medina and Dammam. Many passengers routed through other airports make the final leg of their journey on land, though Riyadh's streets remain busy with restaurants and shopping centres operating undeterred.

Getting people to speak openly about the conflict is difficult because strict censorship laws discourage talking to the media. Those who did express confidence in Saudi Arabia's ability to protect them, even as sudden air-defence alerts interrupt daily life.

The Houthis' renewed offensive has captured territory along the Red Sea coast and threatened routes toward Aden while intensifying fighting around Taiz. Road closures from a Houthi siege there have cut more than 800,000 people off from humanitarian assistance according to Unicef.

More than 360,000 people have been forced from their homes in Yemen since August per the IOM, and the UN Human Rights Office has verified 323 civilian casualties since then including 76 killed with children making up half of the dead. One Saudi-led strike on Sanaa earlier this month reportedly killed 44 people according to Houthi authorities.

A Saudi-led coalition responded to the Houthi advances and attacks with intensified air strikes, which it says aim to protect the Yemeni population and global trade from the Houthis.
items.title: Houthi attacks test Saudi Arabia's image of security

The Australian Federal Police arrested three men over three days in Far North Queensland as part of three separate international child exploitation investigations. The cases involve alleged child abuse connected to Ukraine, the Philippines, and the USA.

Two of the arrested men have been granted bail to appear in local magistrates courts in December, while a third man remains under investigation.
items.title: AFP Arrests Three Men Over International Child Exploitation Cases

China is promoting a nationwide winter tourism campaign that highlights snowy villages in the Altay region of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

The promotion features magical night skies over Altay, fairy-tale streets and ice sculptures in Heilongjiang Province, and rime ice along with skiing and snow rafting in Jilin Province.

Officials are inviting visitors to experience what they describe as China's winter wonderland.
items.title: China Promotes Winter Tourism Across Xinjiang, Heilongjiang, and Jilin

A coronial inquest into the deaths of three people in outback Queensland nearly 50 years ago has concluded, with a man previously charged with their homicide found reasonably suspected of being directly involved. The findings were handed down today in a Brisbane court after evidence was heard in October last year.

Coroner David O'Connell delivered the conclusion that the man was likely connected to the killings during an investigation spanning decades.
items.title: Man Found Likely Involved In 1970s Outback Queensland Murders

Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al Thani arrived in Cairo on Thursday to meet Egypt's President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, underscoring the two nations' alignment on Gaza, Palestinian statehood, and regional stability.

Both leaders stressed implementing the Gaza ceasefire agreement, ensuring humanitarian aid reaches the territory, and beginning reconstruction without delay. They said a two-state solution along 1967 lines is key to lasting peace in the Middle East.

The meeting also covered de-escalating regional tensions and preventing conflicts from widening.

Egypt's Sisi and Qatar's Tamim pledged to strengthen their economic partnership by increasing trade, expanding investment, and deepening cooperation in energy and other mutually beneficial sectors.
items.title: Egypt's Sisi and Qatar's Tamim Discuss Gaza Ceasefire and Regional Stability

Russia has opened a new outdoor ice rink at Moscow's iconic Soviet-era VDNKh exhibition park, billed as the largest artificial ice surface in Europe.

The skating area spans more than 20,000 square metres and can hold almost 5,000 people at once. The complex totals about 68,300 square metres when its surrounding facilities are included.

According to the park's own billing, the rink first opened in 2015 as Europe's largest artificial ice surface.

The skating route follows the exhibition park's main avenue past Pavilion No. 1 and winds around the Friendship of Peoples and Stone Flower fountains.
items.title: Moscow's Expo Park Opens Europe's Largest Outdoor Ice Rink

A Washington Post report found that banned Nvidia Blackwell B300 chips are being openly sold in Huaqiangbei, a Shenzhen electronics market near the villa where US President Donald Trump met Chinese President Xi Jinping at last week's APEC summit. The article attributes this finding to the newspaper.

Vendors quoted prices of around $3 million for servers containing eight Blackwell B300 chips after contacting suppliers, with one vendor citing 20 million yuan and others ranging from $3 million to $3.4 million. The Washington Post reported these figures.

Prices reportedly rose sharply amid tighter US export controls, according to a vendor identified only by his surname, Wu, who told the newspaper that such servers cost around $2 million two months ago.

An equivalent B300 server costs roughly $500,000 to $600,000 in the US, Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution, told Washington Post. The article attributes this comparison to Chan.

The availability of these chips highlights challenges for Washington in enforcing restrictions aimed at preventing China from accessing advanced American technology and maintaining its lead in artificial intelligence, per the report.

Since Nvidia introduced its Blackwell series in 2024, the US has prohibited shipments to China over national security concerns. The article attributes this timeline to the newspaper.

Vendors told the newspaper that restricted chips continue reaching the Chinese market through supply networks involving Hong Kong and other locations. One vendor said customers from Russia and Iran had purchased Nvidia chips for four or five years.

The Washington Post reported that public procurement records show Chinese research institutes and universities continued acquiring export-restricted Nvidia chips through 2025 and 2026, including as recently as last month.

Amid the scandal, Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia CEO but returned to the position just days later. The article attributes this detail to the newspaper.

The Reserve Bank of India appears to be letting the rupee strengthen on returning foreign inflows instead of buying dollars to rebuild its reserves, analysts and sources familiar with RBI's thinking said. The strategy could encourage exporters to sell more dollars, reduce hedging by importers, and ease concerns over currency losses for foreign investors.

Indian equities drew a record $16 billion in foreign inflows in November after nearly two years of selling, giving the central bank an opportunity to rebuild reserves. Yet RBI has largely stayed out of the currency market despite an $80 billion drawdown from its $785.7 billion peak following heavy dollar sales in October.

The rupee's recovery is limited by around $40 billion in forward commitments maturing over the next year, Dhiraj Nim of ANZ Bank said. He added that RBI's immediate priority may be putting exporter hedging on a sustained footing and easing imbalances between importer and exporter hedging, which could require further rupee appreciation.

Nim forecast stiff resistance at 90-91 per dollar for the currency, which traded at 92.62 on Friday. One source said RBI is in 'no hurry' to rebuild reserves and could allow the rupee to appreciate while replenishing reserves if inflows persist. This aligns with Governor Sanjay Malhotra's view that the rupee was undervalued.

The strategy follows a period of sharp weakness: the rupee fell 4.8 per cent in 2025 and another 5.5 per cent in the first 10 months of this year, pressured by nearly $50 billion in foreign equity outflows. Persistent weakness had prompted RBI to curb open currency positions, impose reserve requirements on large hedging transactions, and let oil companies buy dollars directly from its reserves.

Exporter hedging volumes rose sharply over the past week as Indian IT firms renewed hedging of future dollar receivables. A Reuters poll showed investors turned bullish on the rupee for the first time in 18 months, helped by record foreign equity inflows and lower oil prices.

A sustained recovery would give RBI more flexibility to focus monetary policy on domestic growth and inflation rather than currency weakness. Aaron Hurd of State Street Investment Management said credible interest rate moves addressing domestic inflation pressures would ease rupee pressures, calling for two or three more hikes over the coming quarters.

WhatsApp announced it will let users buy and install a data eSIM for international travel directly in the app, keeping them on their existing phone number abroad without needing an airport kiosk or Wi-Fi. The Meta-owned company posted details Thursday about the feature.

The service would roll out to select countries soon, though WhatsApp did not name those markets or provide pricing information. It said it is working with eSIM providers and telecom partners including Jio, Smart Axiata, Smart Communications, and Verizon.

WhatsApp framed the move as an early exploration of eSIMs that makes international use effortless by letting users land in a new country while staying on their same number instead of switching SIM cards or paying roaming fees. Head Kunal Shah described it this way on X.

The company said WhatsApp has more than 3 billion users worldwide, according to Meta.
items.title: WhatsApp to Sell Travel eSIMs In-App With Jio and Verizon Among Partners

The Reserve Bank of India's approval to launch exchange-traded derivatives linked to its corporate debt market has lifted NSE share prices, with the stock gaining around 1% at Rs 2348 on Thursday. The central bank's decision paves the way for the bourse to offer investors an instrument to manage exposure to movements in corporate bond valuations driven by interest rates and credit spreads.

NSE shares have rallied sharply over recent sessions, gaining nearly 35% in the last month according to reported figures. The article attributes this rally to positive investor sentiment toward large cap stocks alongside favourable brokerage ratings.

The stock closed around 1% higher at Rs 2348 on Thursday, extending its winning streak as reported by the outlet. At that price of Rs 2348, NSE has gained approximately 32% over its September IPO issue price of Rs 1785 per share.

NSE became the world's third-largest stock exchange platform with a market capitalisation of $64 billion according to publicly available data cited in the article. The surge made it India's ninth-largest listed company by market value, taking it ahead of Larsen & Toubro at Rs 5.69 lakh crore and Life Insurance Corporation of India at Rs 5.2 lakh crore.
items.title: NSE shares rise nearly 2% after RBI nod for corporate bond index futures

WhatsApp will let users buy and install a data eSIM for international travel directly within the app, keeping their existing phone number abroad without relying on roaming or local SIM kiosks. The Meta-owned company announced the feature in a blog post Thursday.

The service is intended to help travellers access mobile data overseas while retaining WhatsApp's same-number functionality during trips.

WhatsApp said it was working with eSIM providers and telecom partners including Jio, Smart Axiata, Smart Communications and Verizon, and would begin rolling out the feature in select countries soon. The company did not name those countries or provide pricing details.

According to a quote from the announcement, WhatsApp described the service as letting users buy and install an eSIM 'in just a few taps without leaving the app,' so they can keep using it on their same phone number when landing abroad instead of visiting an airport kiosk, searching for Wi-Fi cafés or incurring roaming charges.

WhatsApp Head Kunal Shah characterized the effort as part of the company's early explorations around eSIMs. In a post on X he wrote about what would happen 'if WhatsApp could work anywhere you go in the world without any struggle,' adding that the company is inviting partners to join this mission.

Meta reported that WhatsApp has more than 3 billion users worldwide.
items.title: WhatsApp to Sell Travel eSIMs In-App With Jio Among Partners

Apple removed the AI companion app Talkie from its App Store worldwide after media reports alleged that the product's characters sent sexualized messages to minors.

ABC News and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism reported on Wednesday that Talkie's AI-generated companions had sent sexually inappropriate and abusive messages to children. The report was attributed to those outlets, which did not respond separately to requests for comment.

Talkie is operated by Shanghai-based MiniMax, launched in 2023, and offers a range of chat companions with romantic undertones; the company also runs a Chinese version called Xingye.

The app carries an 18+ rating on both the Apple App Store and Google Play Store, and depending on the country it states that children under 14 or under 16 cannot sign up. Child safety advocates have criticized its lax verification safeguards, which allow users to self-report their age.

MiniMax and Apple did not immediately respond to requests for comment about the removal.
items.title: Apple Removes MiniMax's Talkie Chatbot Over Child Safety Allegations

Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra urged micro, small and medium enterprises to adopt artificial intelligence on Friday, saying productivity gains could lift India's GDP by 11%.

Malhotra said employee productivity in Indian MSMEs is only 26% of that in large domestic industries. He noted just 15% of these firms have adopted AI while merely 5% have integrated it into core operations.

The Governor pointed out that technology investments and workforce skilling could help enterprises cut costs, improve product quality and boost competitiveness. MSMEs contribute nearly 31% to India's GDP and employ over 45 crore people.

Bank credit to MSMEs grew 27% last year versus a compounded annual growth rate of about 19% across the past five years. Malhotra cited regulatory support such as raising the collateral-free lending limit from Rs 10 lakh to Rs 20 lakh, expanding credit guarantees and simplifying working capital rules.

The Account Aggregator framework has facilitated loans worth Rs 3.5 lakh crore while the Unified Lending Interface aims to streamline credit assessments and cut documentation requirements.
items.title: RBI Governor Calls for AI-Led MSME Transformation

OpenAI is testing a system that combines the usage allowances for ChatGPT's regular conversations and Work tasks into a single shared pool, which could cause some paying subscribers to reach their limits sooner. Until now these two features had separate limits; under the new setup both draw from one allowance, so users must divide their available usage between everyday chats and work-related tasks.

OpenAI announced the plan in an email to subscribers, and executive Thibault 'Tibo' Sottiaux confirmed on X that the combined Chat and Work experience has begun rolling out to a small group of Pro users. He said the goal is to gather feedback before a broader release.

An OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch that most users are unlikely to see their usage reset more often, but a small number of heavy users may hit limits sooner—particularly those who use ChatGPT frequently for both casual conversations and demanding work tasks. Reports from tech outlets indicate that more advanced models and complex tasks will consume more of the shared allowance.

Some subscribers have expressed concerns on social media and in OpenAI's community forum, fearing reduced access to advanced reasoning models while paying the same subscription fee. Decrypt reported asking whether subscribers would keep their combined entitlements or receive less usage for the same price; OpenAI had not responded by publication time.

OpenAI said conversations with its Instant model will remain unlimited and won't count toward the shared allowance, so users can continue chatting after exhausting their limit—though only with that basic model. Subscribers will also be able to check their combined remaining usage and reset times in ChatGPT's settings, though OpenAI has not specified how detailed that view will be.

For now only a small group of Pro subscribers have the combined system; OpenAI plans to widen it in December across Plus, Pro, and Business plans. Reports say Codex, its coding tool, would then join the shared pool as well. OpenAI said it intends to keep improving system efficiency so existing plan holders get more value.

The change comes amid strong demand and rising costs for running powerful models at AI companies. OpenAI frames the merger as a simplification that lets users switch between regular conversations and complex tasks in one place. It follows recent adjustments to usage limits, including last month's reversal of a planned cut to Work and Codex allowances on its $200 Pro plan after subscriber backlash, along with doubled limits across its Pro tiers and Business Premium.
items.title: OpenAI Merges ChatGPT Usage Limits Into Shared Pool

Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Friday that the India-US trade deal is close to culmination, with its process and pathway beginning to take shape. He made the remarks while addressing the India Debt Capital Market Summit 2026 virtually.

Goyal framed the recent trade disruptions as an advantage for India's growth story, quoting Harivansh Rai Bachchan on turning adverse situations to benefit 1.4 billion Indians in coming years.

His comments come amid renewed uncertainty after US Trade Representative USTR proposed duties of up to 25% on Indian goods under a Section 301 investigation into alleged structural excess capacity in manufacturing, with the rate potentially reduced to 17% if India reaches a reciprocal trade agreement. New Delhi rejected Washington's allegations and said any concerns should be resolved through ongoing bilateral negotiations.

Goyal also projected that the India-European Union free trade agreement would likely be signed later this year and come into effect by March or April 2027, adding that eight to nine agreements under negotiation could expand market access to economies worth $85 trillion. Over the past five years, India has finalised nine FTAs covering 38 developed countries with a combined GDP of $70 trillion.

India recorded 7.8% growth in the first quarter of the current financial year, with gross fixed capital formation up around 12 per cent and bank credit expanding by nearly 19 per cent. Exports reached about $570 billion over the first seven months, while October exports hit a record near $90 billion, putting India on track to meet its $1 trillion annual export target.
items.title: Goyal says India-US trade deal nears finalisation

Shares of equipment rental company Watrana Rentals jumped 3% after the firm listed at a discount to its IPO price on the NSE SME platform.

The SME offering was a book-built issue worth Rs 120.10 crore, made up entirely of a fresh share sale of about 49.02 lakh shares.

Applications were opened for subscription on November 19 and closed on November 19 to November 23.

Each application lot comprised 600 shares, with retail investors required to apply at least two lots based on the upper price, making the minimum investment Rs 2,94,000.

Net proceeds from the public offering are earmarked for buying material handling equipment, aerial work platforms and batteries, as well as corporate general purposes.
items.title: Watrana Rentals shares rise after discount listing

items.summary:
Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said the India-US trade deal is close to completion, with the process that had stalled negotiations now taking shape. He made the remarks while addressing the India Debt Capital Market Summit virtually.

The statement follows a US Trade Representative report proposing 25 per cent tariffs on Indian imports, capped at 17 per cent if both countries reach a bilateral deal. Goyal has repeatedly said the pact will be signed once that tariff framework is in place and India gains comparative advantage over rival manufacturers such as Bangladesh, Vietnam, Pakistan, Indonesia, Thailand, and China.

Trade experts hope the US Section 301 report could trigger intensive negotiations on the agreement in coming weeks. Goyal also said the India-EU free trade agreement may be signed later this year and come into effect by March or April next year.

Despite global tensions, tariffs, oil shocks, and disrupted shipping routes, Goyal said India's goods and services exports remain on track for a $1 trillion target in the current fiscal. He cited 7.8 per cent growth in Q1 as evidence of continued confidence in India's economy.
items.title: India-US Trade Deal Nearing Completion, Roadmap Taking Shape

Congress MP Imran Masood rejected a call for unity from party chief Mallikarjun Kharge, refusing to soften his criticism of the Samajwadi Party over seat-sharing for Uttar Pradesh. Speaking to news agency ANI on Friday, Masood said he felt cornered and treated as a villain while insisting he would keep raising concerns in Congress's interest.

Masood questioned whether defeating BJP rests solely on him, arguing that responsibility also lies with the Samajwadi Party over its approach to alliance negotiations. He demanded quality seats where Congress can win rather than accepting constituencies it is unlikely to contest successfully.

The dispute intensified after reports that the SP offered 26 seats as a starting point and announced five candidates while talks were ongoing, prompting Masood to say he would not be treated like a beggar being dictated terms. He argued Congress's value in an alliance should not be measured only by past electoral performance.

Congress is reportedly seeking around 130 seats for the proposed alliance, according to reports cited in coverage of the negotiations. The SP's initial offer stood at 26 seats as reported during the discussions.
items.title: Congress MP Masood Defies Kharge Over UP Seat-Sharing With Samajwadi Party

The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed a plea seeking removal of videos showing Italian politician Giacomo Filibeck raising the slogan 'Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod' at a Congress event in Hyderabad.

The court also rejected an accompanying request for an independent SIT probe into foreign delegates' participation and permissions granted to them. The case was heard by Chief Justice Surya Kant during an earlier mentioning.

Petitioner's counsel alleged that PES secretary-general Filibeck interfered in India's domestic politics by criticising the government and backing the Opposition. This claim follows his remarks at Bharat Summit 2026 on November 13-14, where he voiced support for opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and Congress while calling Indian democracy 'under attack.'

Filibeck described himself as part of a progressive alliance across Europe committed to social justice, climate justice, human rights and democracy. The slogan drew criticism from the BJP, which accused Congress of allowing foreign representatives to comment on India's internal affairs.

The Bharat Summit 2026 in Hyderabad brought together around 1,000 delegates, policymakers and thinkers from 70 countries for discussions on geopolitics, democracy, climate change, artificial intelligence and progressive politics.
items.title: Supreme Court Rejects Plea to Remove Italian Politician's 'Vote Chor' Videos

According to an exchange filing, Waaree won an order for the supply of solar modules plus Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) work worth a project scheduled to be completed during financial year 2027-28.

The company said neither its promoters nor promoter group or group companies have any interest in the entity that awarded the order, and it does not fall under related-party dealings.

Union commerce minister Piyush Goyal said the India-US trade deal is close to culmination after processes that had delayed it are now taking shape.

Goyal made the statement at the virtual India Debt Capital Market Summit 2026 on Friday, attributing the delay to some procedures rather than a breakdown in talks.

The remarks follow a US Trade Representative report proposing 25 per cent tariffs on Indian imports, with a provision to cap them at 17 per cent if both countries reach a bilateral deal.

India's trade ministry said it was examining the USTR notice and noted that New Delhi told the US there is no structural excess capacity in any industry during the investigation.

The two nations have had an unsettled trade relationship under the Trump administration, with US tariffs on India changing since April 2025 from 26 per cent to 25 per cent before reaching 50 per cent after a further 25 per cent levy over Russian oil purchases.
items.title: India-US Trade Deal Near Final Stage, Goyal Says

In a 2024 survey of livestock-keeping families around Baramati, Maharashtra, ICAR-NIASM scientists found that seasonal fodder sources were nearly exhausted and that most farmers cited lack of quality feed as their biggest problem. Maize silage supplied about 90% of dry fodder in the kharif season and sorghum about 93% during summer, while roughly 87% of respondents reported fodder scarcity during drought.

The scientists say this local situation mirrors a wider national shortfall: Maharashtra faces an estimated deficit of 31.3% in dry fodder and 59.4% in green fodder, even though fodder crops cover only about 3% of the state's cultivated area according to 2020 estimates by ICAR-Indian Grassland and Fodder Research Institute.

To address this, ICAR-NIASM with NABARD support created CHARA Bank, a perennial fodder system that uses roughly 1,000 square metres (about one-fourth of an acre) of underused land to produce repeated harvests year-round. The approach combines deep-rooted trees and grasses with nitrogen-fixing legumes so the plots draw on deeper soil moisture while improving fertility.

On 21 farmers' fields these systems produced about 9-22 tonnes of green fodder annually from just that small area, and laboratory analysis showed crude protein ranging from 9.3% in Cenchrus grass to 28.2% in Sesbania. The authors note the plots are meant to supplement rather than replace purchased feed.

Dairy animals receiving CHARA Bank green fodder used about 33% less concentrate while milk yield and fat content held steady or rose, an outcome the scientists estimate could add roughly ₹2,670 to ₹26,000 per cow per lactation. Similar gains appeared in Murrah buffaloes and Osmanabadi goats.

The authors attribute adoption growth from 21 lead farmers to more than 150 farmers largely through farmer-to-farmer contact, with hundreds of additional visitors learning the system at field days and exhibitions. They say scaling will depend on collaboration among NABARD, state departments, research institutions and local communities.

CHARA Bank is presented as one option among several suited to different soils and spaces, including irrigated black soil versus shallow murrum and limited spare land versus existing field bunds. The team also noted an initial establishment cost of about ₹15,000-25,000 per 1,000 square metres.

The commentary is written by ICAR-NIASM scientists with NABARD support and its findings are not independently verified; Mongabay-India reports the views as those of the authors.
items.title: CHARA Bank turns underused land into drought-proof fodder in India
