Securities and Exchange Board of India chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey confirmed on Friday that the regulator is examining the Tata Steel–APL Apollo deal, citing its commitment to protecting minority shareholders. The two-part transaction has drawn sharp criticism from minority investors over related-party-transaction structuring and what they view as an unduly lucrative exit for APL Apollo's promoters.

The core of the dispute concerns how the deal was structured so that Tata Steel appeared not to be a related party when APL Apollo's board approved acquiring two businesses worth ₹28,000 crore on Sunday evening. Proxy advisory firms Institutional Investor Advisory Services, Stakeholders Empowerment Services and InGovern argued this arrangement avoided mandatory shareholder approval for related-party transactions.

Under the plan, Tata Steel will pay ₹15,510 crore to buy a 26.38% promoter stake in APL Apollo and launch an open offer for another 26%, raising its potential total outlay to ₹32,266 crore. Investors question whether this structure leaves APL Apollo bearing much of the debt tied to Tata Steel's takeover.

Tata Steel said it has complied with applicable laws but is examining concerns raised by investors and proxy advisors about how best to address them. Pandey noted that proxy firms are meant to raise issues when they feel strongly, while shares of APL Apollo rose 3% on Friday after his remarks.

The Hindu reported that Karnataka's final electoral roll contains more than 17,000 entries where a parent is listed as younger than their child or within an age gap of less than 15 years.

In one example cited by the newspaper, Krishnoji in BBMP South district is recorded at 59 while his son Gowtham appears to be 70. Both are registered at the same house number in polling station 180 of Govindarajanagar Assembly constituency.

Raichur district had the most such discrepancies with about 1,960 entries, ahead of Kalaburagi and Yadgir districts.

The Election Commission treats an age gap under 15 years between parent and child as one of nine categories of logical discrepancy. The commission has asked crores of voters to explain these gaps in order to keep their names on the rolls.

At the draft stage, more than 43 lakh people were served notices over logical discrepancies. Separately, more than 65 lakh voters were marked as permanently shifted, with about 12.3 lakh flagged dead, roughly 15.1 lakh absent and around 7 lakh duplicate entries.

The final roll published on October 27 deleted more than 99.3 lakh names, reducing the state's electorate from 5.5 crore to 4.5 crore, a drop of about 17.9%.

Breaking down the parent-child discrepancies by age gap, The Hindu found at least 2,200 entries where fathers are one to five years younger than their children, more than 5,000 with gaps between six and 10 years, and another 3,000 within a different range.

The Karnataka chief electoral officer's office said it would verify the flagged entries after The Hindu forwarded sample cases.
items.title: Karnataka voter rolls list parents younger than children in thousands of entries

The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) has set two conditions for supporting the Union government's proposed delimitation bill, calling a meeting of its parliamentary members in Chennai ahead of a special Parliament session.

DMK insists Tamil Nadu's 7.18 percent Lok Sabha representation should remain proportional even if total seats increase, according to the party.

The party also requests a 25-year extension on the freeze of interstate seat distribution based on the 1971 census framework.

With 22 Lok Sabha and 8 Rajya Sabha members, DMK plays a crucial role in Parliament amid regional political tensions in Tamil Nadu.
items.title: DMK Sets Conditions to Support Union Government on Delimitation

The Hindi action film 'Gunmaaster G9,' directed by Aditya Datt, was reviewed unfavorably for missing its target through excessive length, gory violence, loud sound design, and weak dialogue.

Running 143 minutes, the movie follows police inspector Rana (Abhishek Singh), who persuades Desu's former enforcer Eeshwar (Emraan Hashmi) to abandon his dairy farming life in order to fight the psychotic gangster Desu (Aparshakti Khurana).

The review criticized composer and singer Himesh Reshammiya for a nasal voice that competes with AutoTune, contributing to an overall cacophony. It also faulted Genelia Deshmukh's character Aarti for pinched dialogue delivery.

Emraan Hashmi was noted as being in maximal swagger mode following the success of 'Awarapan 2,' delivering lines described by the reviewer as edicts rather than sentences, including a garbled threat about killing and laying victims on a pyre. The review attributed this line to Eeshwar's character.

The film references Mithun Chakraborty's James Bond-style role in Ravikant Nagaich's 1979 cult movie 'Surakksha,' which inspired the title, with an added letter presumably intended to attract box office attention. The reviewer also observed that child actor Inayat Verma has since become a teenager and appeared prominently in a scene described as perverse.
items.title: 'Gunmaaster G9': Hindi action film criticized as unfocused and noisy

The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is reviewing amendments to the Delimitation Bill in response to opposition concerns raised ahead of a four-day special Parliament session.

Key proposals under consideration include granting states without population linkage a uniform 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats and separating the delimitation exercise from the census. These measures are intended to safeguard southern states' representation, according to reports.

The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam has requested a 25-year freeze on delimitation as part of its support conditions for backing the bill. The central government dismissed opposition concerns about constitutionality and directed NCP Lok Sabha MPs to attend the session in Delhi.
items.title: Union Cabinet Reviews Amendments to Delimitation Bill

Hindustan Zinc shares rose about 3% Friday, led by a recovery in silver prices after the metal fell more than 60% from its January high.

Silver futures with December 4 expiry climbed nearly 4% to Rs 1,51,439 on Friday, according to Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX) data. The Rajasthan-based Hindustan Zinc is the flagship company of Vedanta and was the biggest gainer among group stocks.

Silver accounts for nearly 45% of Hindustan Zinc's profit after tax, per a report by Kotak Neo, making the metal sensitive to changes in silver prices.

The earlier selloff in silver stemmed from expectations of further US Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, a sharp correction in global equities that prompted investors to liquidate precious metals for cash, and continued outflows from silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

Hindustan Zinc shares advanced nearly 4% over the last five trading sessions and 10% in the past month. However, they are down about 17% over six months and 11% on a year-to-date basis.
items.title: Hindustan Zinc shares gain as silver prices recover

Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath ridiculed the Samajwadi Party's pledge to provide 2.5 million government jobs in five years, urging young voters to examine what the party accomplished during its own tenures.

Adityanath said his BJP government distributed 9.75 lakh government appointments over nine and a half years, which he contrasted with four SP terms (2012-2017) combined with three BSP terms (2007-2017).

On pensions, the chief minister argued that the New Pension Scheme was introduced in 2005 under the Samajwadi Party government and criticized it as being rolled out by the party now attacking his scheme.

He said approximately 8 lakh new pension accounts had been opened when he took power in 2017, adding that no single pension account was opened for employees during either the BSP or SP periods between 2007 and 2017.

The remarks were made at a government function where appointment letters were distributed to 1,594 newly selected auditors and assistant accountants in the Directorate of Internal Audit and Accounts.

Adityanath also cited law-and-order improvements under his government, recalling that an IT firm he visited with around 100 employees had grown its workforce to 18,000 over nine years.

The article was written by Rajeev Mullick, a Lucknow-based journalist who headed the Lucknow City Bureau from 2012 to 2024 and has covered governance and public policy in Uttar Pradesh for more than 26 years.
